These official SARS sources, fetched and read in full, show that essentially all revenue types — personal/corporate income tax, VAT, PAYE/SDL/UIF, provisional tax, transfer duty, securities transfer tax, withholding taxes, air passenger tax, excise duties (fuel, tobacco, alcohol, carbon tax, etc.) and customs duties/VAT — are payable electronically via eFiling (Credit Push), EFT, the SARS MobiApp, or SWIFT for foreign payers, and that Customs and Excise clients required to declare electronically are in fact mandated to pay via eFiling under the Customs and Excise Act No. 91 of 1964. Cheques were discontinued as a payment method from Dec 2020 (Customs) / Jan 2021 (banks). revised_comments: South Africa's Revenue Service (SARS) supports comprehensive digital payment of government revenue. Practically all tax types — personal and corporate income tax, VAT, PAYE/SDL/UIF, provisional tax, transfer duty, securities transfer tax, withholding taxes, air passenger tax and excise duties (including fuel, tobacco, alcohol and carbon tax) — together with customs duties, can be paid electronically via SARS eFiling (Credit Push), Electronic Funds Transfer with SARS-prefixed beneficiary IDs, the SARS MobiApp, or SWIFT transfer for foreign taxpayers without a South African bank account. Customs and excise clients required to declare goods electronically are in fact mandated to pay via eFiling under the Customs and Excise Act, No. 91 of 1964. Cheque payments were discontinued at Customs ports of entry from December 2020 and at banks from January 2021, reflecting a full shift to digital revenue collection.
